oracle.bow: src/sites.js: the bow stem is solid at x 14..16, dTop 28 (line 322); the main deck is a structure from x 22 to 78 at d 27..28 (line 327), after the bow-visor opening (comment, line 326); the visor is a bowVisor feature at (18, 26) (line 449), drawn by src/renderer.js drawBowVisor (line 5806) as a 72 by 20 px slab (3.6 by 1 m at 0.05 m/px), hinged up. src/renderer.js drawWreckEntryMarkers marks the BOW entry from above at x 16..22 on the main-deck line (line 4962). overheadAt (src/sites.js line 977) is true when a structure with its bottom above the diver spans its x: from x 22 under the deck, never in the opening at the vehicle-deck depth. Legacy's zone map (visualZones, src/sites.js line 560) puts the vehicle deck, an interior zone, at x 14..170, d 28..40, so it disagrees with overheadAt in the opening.
oracle.engine: src/sites.js lines 503..508: the engines are site features ({kind:'engine'}), not structures; solidAt, solidBoxAt and solidOverlapArea iterate only s.structures, so legacy's diver swims through its engines. The migration client departs from that by the owner's decision, recorded in docs/decisions.md (Deliberate departures).
oracle.visor: src/sites.js line 449: the bow visor is a site feature ({kind:'bowVisor'}) at (18, 26), drawn by src/renderer.js drawBowVisor (line 5806) and never collided with. The migration draws it on the deck's forward edge (x 22..23) and makes it solid, by the owner's decision on #222 ("whatever looks better"), recorded in docs/decisions.md (Deliberate departures).

parityTest.legacy: The real src/sites.js through ?raw and a Function body, as tests/parity/site-geometry.test.ts loads it (no node:vm: the project has no node APIs or @types/node); legacy's own solidAt and overheadAt with the wreck selected.
parityTest.grid: x 8..99 every 0.25 m. Each column is split into three bands, and a migration depth is mapped linearly onto legacy's in its band: above the deck (surface to the deck's top) onto legacy's 0..27 m, the deck (top to underside) onto 27..28 m, the hold (underside to the hold's floor, 33.5 m) onto 28..39 m, legacy's vehicle deck (src/sites.js lines 327 and 358). Ahead of the deck the drawing's band edges are those at its forward edge. Samples sit at cell centres, 40, 6 and 44 cells, so none lands on a band edge, where legacy's edges are inclusive.
parityTest.assertions: Solid equals legacy's solidAt at every compared sample outside the two declared regions; inside them the migration is solid and legacy is not, and each region is actually sampled (visor over 20 samples, engine over 200). The overhead equals legacy's overheadAt wherever both are in open water (over 10000 samples). Legacy's bowVisor (x 18) and its six engines are features, and legacy's diver is free where each is drawn.
parityTest.regions: Written in the test as numbers with their legacy sources, not read from WRECK_VISOR or WRECK_ENGINE. The visor: x 22..23 (legacy's main deck's x1, src/sites.js line 327, and the slab's 1 m from drawBowVisor's 20 px at 0.05 m/px), above the deck from 23 - 3.6 m (drawBowVisor's 72 px). The engine block: legacy's engines (lines 503..508; drawEngine, src/renderer.js line 5644, 88 by 64 px) are neither at the drawing's place nor of its size, so the region is the provisional drawing's engine written out, in the hold: a cylinder of radius 3.1 about (87, 30.5) and a bed from x 81 to 95 below 33 m.
parityTest.excluded: Where the provisional drawing does not model legacy's wreck (#240): above the deck from x 40 (legacy's superstructure, src/sites.js line 334); the deck band over legacy's main hatch, 78 < x < 92, where legacy's deck is open; the overhead past x 78 (the hatch); and past x 99 (the drawing's stern wall at 99..103). Solid in the hold is compared over the whole range, the hatch included, which is where the engine block lies.
parityTest.checkpoints: The test reads the wreck scenarios of tests/fixtures/traces/baseline-v1.json and names them: trimix-45m-20min, tec-switch-21m, trimix-dcs-above-stop, trimix-dcs-surfaced (all checkpoints at diverX_m 0) and wreck-thirds (surface at x 50, 0 m; outbound-10min, turn-20min and reserve-28min at x 50, 32 m; outside-29min at x -20, 32 m). It asserts that no checkpoint lies at the visor's x 22..23 or the engine block's x 81..95, at any depth. The three wreck-thirds hold checkpoints are compared with legacy through the band mapping (32 m maps to 23.8 + 9.7 * 4/11, about 27.33 m, under the drawn deck): not solid and in the overhead in both. The rest are outside the compared range, and the test lists them: x 0 and -20 are before the route's start at 8, and wreck-thirds/surface (x 50, 0 m) is above the deck past x 40.

implemented: src/sites/wreck-route.ts: the deck's underside starts at x 22 with the deck (was 27); CARGO_HOLD_FROM_M 27 -> 22; WRECK_HOLD_BOW_X_M 21 -> 16, the stem's after face; WRECK_STEM_TOP_M 24.5, level with the deck's underside as legacy's stem top is with its deck's; routeSpacesAt ahead of the deck: open water to 34 m before x 14, water to the stem's top over x 14..16, water to the hold's floor (33.5 m) in the opening x 16..22, all outside the overhead; WRECK_VISOR, the raised visor standing on the deck's forward edge (x 22..23, from 19.4 m to the deck), solid; WRECK_ENGINE and engineTopAt, the cylinder and its bed setting the floor under the deck. The Pixi renderer and the dev canvas adapter draw the hull and the hold from the shared WRECK_HULL_EDGE and WRECK_HOLD_EDGE, stroked as open paths so no line closes the opening; the engine from WRECK_ENGINE; the guideline over the stem, down the opening and over the engine. src/app/game-controller.ts is unchanged.
gameplayEffect: The dive still starts at route position 10, open water from the surface to 34 m. A diver level below 24.5 m off the bow is stopped by the stem; the hold is entered by crossing the stem above 24.5 m, sinking in the opening and swimming aft under the deck from x 22, where the overhead, the rule of thirds and the Cargo hold readout begin. In the opening the HUD reads Wreck exterior, following legacy's overheadAt rather than its zone map. The engine block stops the diver, who goes over its top at 27.4 m.
